$comment: Prompt and instruction security, Standard 21. This is the standard with no existing owner anywhere in the portfolio: MachineLearningStandards has no prompt-as-subject content, and EngineeringStandards' ai.* rules govern agents building software rather than prompts inside a product.

rules.title: System prompts are versioned files, not inline literals
rules.description: A system prompt is stored as a committed file that can be diffed, reviewed and rolled back, rather than as a string literal at a call site.
rules.rationale: A prompt is the largest untested surface in most AI systems and the one most often changed without review. A literal buried in a call site has no version, no reviewer and no rollback, and changing it changes system behaviour more than most code changes do.
rules.remediation: Move the prompt to a file under a prompts directory and load it by reference.
rules.$assuranceNote: Literal recognition only. A prompt assembled from concatenated fragments or fetched at runtime is invisible here, so absence of a finding is not evidence that prompts are file-backed. A clean result therefore reports not-evaluated, never passed.

rules.title: No long instruction literal sits at a model call site
rules.description: Instruction text passed to a model is not an inline literal at the call site.
rules.rationale: This is the advisory face of promptsec.prompt-is-versioned-artifact. It is recommended rather than required because a short inline instruction is sometimes the honest shape of a small system, and a required rule here would be turned off rather than met.
rules.remediation: Extract the literal to a prompt file.
rules.$assuranceNote: Same recognition as promptsec.prompt-is-versioned-artifact, reported at warning severity.

rules.title: A prompt-injection threat model exists
rules.description: A threat model records where untrusted content enters the instruction path and what bounds its authority.
rules.rationale: Prompt injection is not a bug class that testing finds incidentally. A system with no written trust boundary has one anyway; it is just unstated and therefore unreviewed.
rules.remediation: Write a threat model covering prompt, tool, retrieval and agent surfaces.

rules.title: Secrets never enter model context
rules.description: API keys, tokens and credentials are never placed into a prompt, a context window, or a retrieved document.
rules.rationale: A secret in a context window is a secret in every trace, every log, every eval fixture and every provider's retention window, and it is extractable by the injection this pack's other rules exist to bound.
rules.remediation: Pass credentials through the tool layer, never through model context.
rules.$exemptibilityNote: There is no system that legitimately needs a credential inside model context. Where a tool needs one, the tool holds it.

rules.title: Prompt templates resist injection through interpolated values
rules.description: Values interpolated into a prompt template cannot acquire instruction authority.
rules.rationale: Whether a guard holds is a property of the model's behaviour on adversarial input, not a property of the guard's source code.
rules.remediation: Establish this through a recorded red-team exercise rather than by inspection.
rules.$notEvaluableNote: The subject is whether the model treats interpolated content as instruction, which is behaviour at inference time and not repository content. It becomes checkable only through a recorded red-team artifact produced by a named harness at a recorded revision, which a separate rule would then examine; no rule in this release does. Reading the guard establishes that someone wrote a guard, never that it holds.
